bull.b: Growth across both MedSurg and Neurotechnology and Orthopaedics demonstrates a broad revenue base rather than dependence on one product area. This diversification, supported by procedure-driven demand and international expansion, can improve resilience and sustain growth over the next several quarters.

High gross and operating margins indicate meaningful profitability from Stryker’s medical technology portfolio, while substantial free cash flow supports product development, acquisitions, debt management and shareholder returns. These economics provide capacity to keep investing through changing procedure environments.

Stryker is extending its competitive position through acquisitions, robotics, AI and a broad pipeline of devices and procedures. New technologies such as FiberLocker and Versius expand the addressable market, while the Mako ecosystem and future launches can deepen customer adoption.

bear.b: Slower hip and knee procedure growth directly pressures one of Stryker’s important orthopaedic franchises. Affordability concerns, pre-authorization denials and regional softness may constrain volumes for several quarters, reducing the benefit of the company’s established implant and instrument positions.

Continuing supply disruption in Peripheral Vascular is limiting the company’s ability to convert demand into sales and can weaken customer availability. Even with sequential improvement, the issue may remain a drag on growth until inventory and product availability normalize fully.

Execution challenges are limiting Stryker’s ability to outperform the orthopaedics market despite its strong franchise and technology portfolio. Delayed visibility, operational distractions and slower new-product adoption could weigh on share gains, growth durability and near-term margin leverage.
